title: David Bennett at Accelerate Tomorrow AI Summit 2026 in Berlin
description: David Bennett spoke at Accelerate Tomorrow AI Summit 2026 in Berlin about digital humans, AI avatars and practical human-AI interaction.
body:
How do digital humans fit into the next wave of enterprise AI?

2–3 June 2026 | Estrel Berlin | Speaker

David Bennett joined the Accelerate Tomorrow AI Summit at Estrel Berlin, where executives, technology leaders and AI practitioners met to discuss how artificial intelligence is moving from experiments into real products and workflows.

His contribution brought a character-production perspective to the discussion. Digital humans combine conversational AI with a visible, expressive interface that can speak, respond and guide an interaction in real time.

Digital humans as an AI interface

Most AI tools are still experienced through text boxes, dashboards or voice assistants. A digital human adds a face, voice and consistent character to the system. This can make complex information easier to present when trust, clarity and social presence matter.

The useful question is not whether an avatar looks impressive. It is whether the character helps someone complete a task, understand information or take part in an experience with less friction.

What production-ready interaction requires

A working digital human needs more than a language model. Facial animation, voice, timing, rendering, memory and conversation rules have to operate as one system. When these layers fall out of sync, the experience quickly feels artificial.

David’s background in visual effects, performance capture and digital character production gives him a practical view of this problem. The goal is a reliable interface that can hold a clear role in training, live events, customer experience or immersive environments.

Why the summit mattered

Accelerate Tomorrow connected technical development with real business use cases. David’s appearance placed digital humans within that wider enterprise AI conversation, alongside questions about implementation, responsibility and measurable value.

title: The Human Within the Machine: David Bennett’s IFA Berlin 2026 Keynote
description: David Bennett presented “The Human within the Machine” at IFA Berlin’s 2026 Kick-Off, with a live Mimic digital human demonstration.
body:
What makes a digital human feel understandable, responsive and human?

30 June 2026 | Futurium Berlin | Keynote and Mimic demonstration booth

David Bennett delivered the keynote “Mimic - The Human within the Machine” at the IFA Berlin 2026 Kick-Off at Futurium Berlin. Mimic Productions also presented a live demonstration at its booth.

The keynote explored how digital humans are changing from visual assets into live interfaces that can listen, speak, gesture and respond in real time.

The human layer in an AI system

People do not experience an AI system only through its underlying model. They experience its timing, voice, expressions, movement and behaviour. A digital human gives those elements a visible form.

That visible form can make an interaction easier to understand, but it also creates responsibility. The character should be clearly identified as digital, stay consistent with its intended role and avoid suggesting abilities it does not have.

From keynote to live demonstration

The Mimic booth showed how the ideas discussed on stage can work in practice. A production-ready digital human requires character design, animation, speech, conversational logic and real-time rendering to operate as one system.

A live demonstration also exposes the practical details that edited videos can hide, including response time, turn-taking, facial timing and the stability of the complete pipeline.

Why IFA was the right setting

The IFA Kick-Off brought media, consumer technology leaders and innovators together before IFA 2026. It gave David a setting to connect advances in AI with the way people will actually encounter digital characters in products, services and public experiences.

title: From AI Avatars to Agentic Digital Humans: David Bennett at Agentic AI Summit Berlin
description: David Bennett explained the shift from AI avatars to agentic digital humans at Agentic AI Summit Berlin on 15 September 2026.
body:
What changes when an AI avatar can understand context and act?

15 September 2026, 14:30–15:00 | The Ritz-Carlton Berlin | Speaker

David Bennett spoke at Agentic AI Summit Berlin in a session titled “From AI avatars to agentic digital humans: The next interface for human-AI interaction.”

The session examined the shift from text-based chat interfaces towards embodied systems that can speak, respond, remember context and interact in real time.

What is an agentic digital human?

An agentic digital human combines a visual character, conversational AI and a system that can take context-aware actions. It is not simply a face placed over a chatbot.

Speech, facial animation, gesture, memory, turn-taking and safeguards need to work together. The character also needs a clearly defined role so people understand what it can do and where its limits are.

The interface has to feel coherent

Visual quality is only one part of the experience. Low latency, natural timing and consistent behaviour matter just as much. If the voice, expression and response do not align, the interaction loses credibility.

David connected these requirements to Mimic’s work in real-time characters and conversational avatars, showing how character production and AI systems meet in a practical deployment.

Where agentic digital humans can be useful

The format is relevant when people benefit from a visible, social presence. Examples include entertainment, training, customer experience, guided information and immersive environments.

The character should support a real task. A clear use case, transparent behaviour and appropriate human oversight matter more than novelty.

title: David Bennett at LEaT con 2026: AI Avatars, Holograms and Digital Humans
description: David Bennett will speak at LEaT con 2026 about AI avatars, holograms and digital humans for live entertainment and immersive events.
body:
How will AI avatars and digital humans change live entertainment?

6–8 October 2026 | Hamburg Messe | Speaker

David Bennett was announced as a speaker at LEaT con 2026, the Hamburg event connecting live technology, stage technology, broadcast, installation and communication.

His appearance focuses on AI avatars, holograms and digital humans in live entertainment, including the move from prerecorded visual effects towards responsive characters and real-time performance.

Why digital humans matter for live entertainment

A digital human can act as a host, performer, guide or interactive character. The technical challenge is not only to make the character look convincing. Voice, animation, conversational behaviour and rendering also have to work reliably in front of a live audience.

For entertainment teams, this creates new options for concerts, installations, exhibitions, brand experiences and hybrid events.

Holograms need more than a visual effect

A holographic presentation becomes more useful when the character can react to a presenter, performer or audience. This requires a production system that connects the displayed character with real-time speech, motion and conversational control.

The creative direction still matters. Technology should support the story or experience instead of becoming a distraction from it.

David Bennett’s perspective

David founded Mimic Productions, a Berlin studio working with digital humans, character production, performance capture and interactive AI avatars. His LEaT con appearance brings that production experience into the practical demands of live entertainment.

The discussion also raises questions about latency, authorship, audience trust and the balance between automated systems and human performance.

title: We Turned Cate Blanchett Into a Singing Tiger
description: Discover how 'We Turned Cate Blanchett Into a Singing Tiger' in Julian Rosefeldt's Euphoria. Dive into the surreal transformation now!
body:
There are moments in this industry where you step back and think — we actually made that. Standing in the Kino International watching Euphoria with an audience, this was one of those moments.

Julian Rosefeldt's Euphoria is not a quiet film. It is bold, surreal, and unashamedly ambitious - a cinematic installation that wrestles with capitalism, desire, excess, and the systems that shape the way we live. It puts remarkable performers in extraordinary situations and asks them to carry enormous ideas with their bodies and voices. The result is something that has to be seen to be believed.

And somewhere inside that film, there is a tiger. A tiger that sings. A tiger that is, unmistakably, Cate Blanchett.

How We Built the Tiger

Our team at Mimic Productions was brought in to handle the facial motion capture, rigging, and animation for this scene. The brief was clear in its creative ambition and demanding in its technical execution: take Cate Blanchett's live performance, every flicker of expression, every nuance of her voice and face, and transfer it faithfully into a photorealistic digital tiger.

We used our proprietary facial capture pipeline to track her performance in precise detail - not just the broad strokes, but the micro-movements that carry emotion. From there, our rigging team built a custom facial rig for the tiger, designed from the ground up to respond to the captured data without losing the feline anatomy that made the character believable. Then animation took over, using the rig and the data together to bring the performance to life.

The goal was never to create a digital animal. The goal was to preserve a human performance inside one - and have audiences feel both at the same time.

We worked closely with Syreal Entertainment throughout, ensuring every creative decision stayed true to Julian's vision for the scene. The surrealism of the film depends on the tiger feeling completely real while also clearly carrying a human soul. That tension - between the feral and the familiar - had to be present in every frame.

Seeing It in the Room

Attending the screening at Kino International was something special in its own right. The venue itself carries weight - a landmark of 1960s GDR architecture that recently reopened in Berlin,. There is something fitting about screening a film this bold in a space with that much history.

After the screening, the full team came on stage - performers, crew, creative collaborators - against rolling end credits that included David Bennett - Mimic Productions GmbH. Seeing our names up there alongside Giancarlo Esposito, Cate Blanchett, and everyone who made this production possible was a genuine privilege.

This is what the work is for. Not just the technical precision or the pipeline efficiency, but the moment when it lands in front of an audience and does something to them. Euphoria did something to that room. And we were part of making that happen.

Grateful to Julian Rosefeldt and the whole production for trusting us with such an extraordinary piece of character work. Proud of everyone at Mimic who poured their craft into it.
